sanskrit: śītijalā iti śītā vātā upā vāntu | himenāgnir āvṛto himenāgniḥ parīvṛtaḥ ||
english: "Cold-watered" — so let the cold winds blow hither. By frost is Agni enveloped; by frost is Agni encompassed on all sides.

sanskrit: ya(t) tvā devā apārundhann ā samudram adhāvayaḥ | himo jaghāna goajaṃ himo akṣaṃ himaś chadiḥ ||
english: When the gods drove you away, you ran all the way to the sea. Frost slew the cow and the goat; frost [slew] the axle; frost [slew] the roof-thatch.

sanskrit: himād adhi pra yāmasi hime adya vimocanam | yam avaṭaṃ śatadaram avaindha saptavadhraye ||
english: From frost we go forth; today release is in the frost. The pit of a hundred hollows that was kindled for the seven eunuchs (saptavadhri).

sanskrit: avakā tatra rohatu khade pari bilaṃ tava | arciṣ ṭe agne prathamam aṅgārām̐ aparām̐ uta ||
english: Let the avakā-plant grow there; around your pit is a hollow. The first [part] of your blaze, O Agni, is flame; the latter part is coals.

sanskrit: gṛbhṇāmi brahmaṇā nāma dhāmadhāma paruṣparuḥ | śītikā nāma te mātā jalāṣo nāma te pitā ||
english: By the power of brahman I seize your name, abode by abode, joint by joint. Śītikā is the name of your mother; Jalāṣa is the name of your father.

sanskrit: iha tvam antarā bhava bāhikam astu yad rapaḥ | hime jātodake vṛddhā sindhutas pary ābhṛtā | tayā te agrabhaṃ nāma- -aśvam ivāśvābhidhānyā ||
english: Be here within; let whatever harm there is remain outside. Born in frost, grown in water, brought all around from the Sindhu — by her I have seized your name, as a horse-tamer seizes a horse with the halter.

sanskrit: āmā nāmāsy oṣadhe tasyās te nāma jagrabha | agastyasya putrāso mā vi dhāk puruṣān mama ||
english: Your name, O herb, is Āmā ("the moist one"); I have seized that name of yours. May the sons of Agastya not scatter my people.

sanskrit: mā no agne tanvaṃ mā vāsāṃsi rīriṣaḥ | yaṃ tvā samudraja vayam ārohāma svastaye ||
english: Do not harm our bodies, O Agni; do not harm our garments — you who are born of the sea, upon whom we mount for our welfare.

sanskrit: divas tārā avāpadran dhārāt samudriyā apaḥ | hiraṇyakumbho harito 'vakābhiḥ parivṛtas tenāgniṃ śamayāmasi ||
english: Stars fell from the sky; sea-waters [poured] from a stream. A golden jar, green, surrounded by avakā-plants — with that we quench Agni.

sanskrit: śamayāmy arcir agneḥ śivas tapatu mā vi dhāk | gṛbhīte dyāvāpṛthivī gṛbhītaṃ pārthivaṃ rajaḥ ||
english: I quench the flame of Agni; may he burn auspiciously, may he not scatter. Sky and Earth are seized; the earthly dust is seized.

sanskrit: ni muñjeṣu yad udakaṃ ni naḍeṣu yad antaram | yat samudre yat sindhau tenāgniṃ śamayāmasi ||
english: The water that lies within muñja-reeds, the water that is within naḍa-reeds, what [abides] in the sea, what in the river — with that we quench Agni.

sanskrit: vetasasyāvakāyā naḍasya vīraṇasya ca | rohitakasya vṛkṣasya- -agniṃ śamanam ud bhare ||
english: From the vetasa-cane, from the avakā-plant, from the naḍa-reed, and from the vīraṇa-grass, and from the rohitaka-tree — I bring forth the quenching of Agni.

sanskrit: āyatīr udahāryo vi te harantu yad rapaḥ | parāyatīḥ parāvataḥ parā harantu yad rapaḥ ||
english: May [the waters] coming hither, as bearers of water, carry away from you whatever harm there is. May [the waters] going away, [going] to the far distance, carry far away whatever harm there is.

sanskrit: himasya tvā jarāyuṇa- -agne pari vyayāmasi | śītike śītam it karo himike himam it karaḥ ||
english: With the afterbirth of frost, O Agni, we wrap you all around. O Śītikā, make it cold indeed; O Himikā, make it frosty indeed.

sanskrit: akṣaṇvatā lāṅgalena padvatā patayiṣṇunā | lāṅgūlagṛhya carkṛṣur vṛkeṇa yavam aśvinā ||
english: With an axle-bearing plow, with a footed, flying one, seizing [it] by the tail — the Aśvins plowed barley together with a wolf.

sanskrit: devā etaṃ madhunā saṃyutaṃ yavaṃ sarasvatyām adhi vaṇāv acarkṛṣuḥ | indra āsīt sīrapatiḥ śatakratuḥ kināśā āsan marutaḥ sudānavaḥ ||
english: The gods plowed this barley mingled with honey on the sandbank of the Sarasvatī. Indra of a hundred powers was lord of the plow; the Maruts, good-givers, were the plowmen.

sanskrit: hiraṇyayaṃ kalaśaṃ sudānavo divyayā saraghayā kṛtam | ava bhṛtam aśvinā yavaṃ tad yuvaṃ madhu cakrathuḥ ||
english: A golden vessel, made by the divine bee, the good-givers — the Aśvins brought down that barley; you two made it [into] honey.

sanskrit: kṛśāv etad ajayatam aśvinā sāraghaṃ madhu | tato yavo vy arohat so 'bhavad viṣadūṣaṇaḥ ||
english: You two, grown lean, won this honey of the bee, O Aśvins. From that the barley grew up; it became the destroyer of poison.

sanskrit: yuvārvān saraghāyāḥ prakhidya madhv ābharat | (…) ||
english: The young one, digging [into] the bee's [hive], brought the honey hither. [The rest of the refrain is as above.]

sanskrit: yad vṛkaṃ madhupāvānam avāmayatam aśvinā | (…) ||
english: When you two, O Aśvins, healed the wolf that had drunk honey. [The rest of the refrain is as above.]

sanskrit: kairaṇḍā nāma saraso vṛkasya vamyā adhi | tato yavo vy arohat so 'bhavad viṣadūṣaṇaḥ ||
english: On the lake named Kairaṇḍā, from the wolf's vomit — from that the barley grew up; it became the destroyer of poison.

sanskrit: yad asya bharatho madhu saraghā sathv acchinat | sadyas tad arvato yuvaṃ punar ā dattam aśvinā ||
english: When the bee cut through the honey that it was carrying as [its] load, thereupon you two, O Aśvins, gave it back at once to the horse.

sanskrit: yo yavaṃ digdhaviddho ahidaṣṭa upāsarat | tīrthe radhram iva majjantam ut taṃ bharatam aśvinā ||
english: He who, struck by a poisoned arrow, bitten by a serpent, comes near — him who sinks at a ford like a helpless one, lift him up, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: yaṃ vahanty aṣṭāyogāḥ ṣaḍyogā yaṃ caturgavāḥ | sa te viṣaṃ vi bādhatām ugro madhyamaśīr iva ||
english: That [barley] which eight yoke-teams carry, which six yoke-teams carry, which four oxen carry — may that one drive away your poison, the mighty one in the midst of the meal, like [a flame consuming it].

sanskrit: yasya yava prasarpasy aṅgamaṅgaṃ paruṣparuḥ | tasmād yakṣaṃ vi bādhasva- -ugro madhyamaśīr iva ||
english: O barley, [from the body] into which you creep, limb by limb, joint by joint — from that one drive away the yakṣma-disease, O mighty one, in the midst of the meal, like [a flame].

sanskrit: śakalaṃ ca na te yava- -anyā ruhanty oṣadhīḥ | yava id yāvayād gor aśvāt puruṣād viṣam ||
english: Not even a shard of you [remains], O barley, [when] other herbs grow up. Barley alone shall drive away poison from cow, from horse, from man.

sanskrit: yavo rājā yavo bhiṣag yavasya mahimā mahān | yavasya manthaṃ papivān indraś cakāra vīryam ||
english: Barley is king; barley is physician; great is the greatness of barley. Having drunk the stirred gruel (mantha) of barley, Indra performed his heroic deed.

sanskrit: ā bharāmṛtaṃ ghṛtasya puṣpam ā bhara | anabhrikhāta oṣadha idaṃ dūṣaya yad viṣam ||
english: Bring hither the immortal bloom of ghee — bring it hither. O herb dug without a spade, corrupt this poison that is here.

sanskrit: ya āyanti digdhaviddhāḥ śūdrā rājanyā uta | cakṣur me sarva ādṛśya te yanty agadāḥ punaḥ ||
english: Those who come struck by poisoned arrows — both Śūdras and Rājanya men — all appearing before my eyes, they go back free of disease.
